custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active, tracked part, part A, for this test with a Core Charge of $25.00, so it has a core described Core for followed by part A's description.
  • Create a part, part B, for this test with a Core Charge of $25.00, then set it inactive and turn its tracking off, so its core is inactive and untracked too.
  • Make sure the Search box in the top bar is the global search, which lists inventory parts.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C847728-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C847728-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • To set a part inactive: on the Inventory page's Active tab click Search, type its part number, click its row; in Edit Inventory Part click Inactive under Part Status, click Save, then click Deactivate in the Deactivate part? window. The part then shows on the Inactive tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The global search opens.

Step 2:

  • No result is listed for part A's core.

Step 3:

  • Part A is listed once, as itself, with its stock badge: there is no second result for its core.

Step 4:

  • No result is listed for part B's core, although it is inactive and untracked.

Step 5:

  • Part B is listed once, with the grey "Inactive" tag and "Not Tracked": its core is not listed beside it.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S9-R18a: “Global search never lists a core, active or inactive, tracked or untracked, as today.”
  • S9-R18: “Global search lists inactive parts at the current location. Each carries the grey "Inactive" tag.”
  • S9-R20: “Global search shows "Not Tracked" for an untracked part, in place of its "{n} available" badge.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “A core always has the same active state and the same tracking state as the part it belongs to.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 13: “(b) No. Global search never lists a core, active or inactive, tracked or not, the same as today (S9-R18a).”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.
